prices.title: Electricity prices
prices.description: Choose a forecast sensor, or a core Nord Pool integration and market area. Native Nord Pool uses EUR spot prices; configure markup, energy tax and VAT. Netting switches to spot compensation on its end date. Spot export requires a raw energy component or a source explicitly configured as spot-only. Before tomorrow's prices are published (around 13:00) the plan uses estimated prices up to 36 h ahead: from an optional external price forecast sensor (calibrated against the published prices), otherwise from a built-in model that learns from past prices, your solar forecast and the wind forecast of the weather entity. Estimates only steer the plan; they are never executed.

pv.title: Solar forecast
pv.description: Forecast sensors (Solcast day sensors, Forecast.Solar, Open-Meteo Solar Forecast). Values from all selected sensors are added up; Solcast's tomorrow and day 3 sensors are added automatically. Production sensors measure what all PV actually produces (for example AC-coupled inverter + MPPTs): used to correct the forecast for clouds and to report forecast accuracy.

data.pv_production_entities: PV production power sensors (all arrays, summed)

load.title: Consumption & grid
load.description: The load forecast uses the recorder history of the consumption sensor (household AC loads, without battery). Grid power sensor: positive = import.

data.import_energy_entity: Cumulative grid import (optional, select both meters)
data.export_energy_entity: Cumulative grid export (optional, select both meters)

control.title: Victron ESS control
control.description: Automatic control requires a grid setpoint and charge, inverter and feed-in limits. Incomplete setups remain advisory with an explanation in Repairs. A configured DESS mode must acknowledge off before ESS commands are sent.

data.dess_mode_entity: Victron Dynamic ESS mode (switched off while in control)

heat_pump.title: Heat pump (SG Ready / EVU)
heat_pump.description: Optional. Energy Control blocks the heat pump (EVU) in expensive quarters when the catch-up afterwards is clearly cheaper, and can use comfort/boost when energy is nearly free. Use a select with SG Ready modes (options containing Normal, EVU/Block, Comfort, Boost are recognised) or a switch/relay. The allowed block length shrinks with the outdoor temperature: full length at the 'full length from' temperature, none at the minimum. Disable other automations that set the same entity, and turn on 'Heat pump control' to start.

data.hp_control_entity: Heat pump mode entity (select or switch)
data.indoor_min_temp: Never block below this indoor temperature
data.hp_comfort: Use comfort mode when energy is cheap
data.hp_boost: Use boost mode (only if the heat pump supports it)

ev.title: EV charger
ev.description: Optional. Smart mode charges in the cheapest quarters (exported PV counts at the export price) before the ready-by time. With an EV state-of-charge sensor and capacity the energy needed follows from the target SoC; otherwise set 'EV energy to charge', which counts down while charging.

error.hp_options: The select has no recognisable Normal and EVU/Block options.

replan.name: Replan
replan.description: Recompute the schedule now (also refreshes the load profile).

override.name: Override
override.description: Run a fixed action for a while, ignoring the plan (control modes only).

cheapest_window.name: Cheapest window
cheapest_window.description: Find the cheapest time to run an appliance (dishwasher, washing machine, EV). Uses the plan: PV that would be exported counts at the export price.

latest_end.name: Ready by
latest_end.description: Latest end time (default: end of known prices).

contiguous.name: In one go
contiguous.description: Off: the cheapest quarters may be spread out (EV charging).

control_failed.title: Energy Control cannot control the ESS
control_failed.description: ESS commands are paused: {error}. Check actuator availability, power units and ranges, and DESS readback. Original settings remain saved for recovery.

load_fallback_no_entity.title: Energy Control has no consumption history
load_fallback_no_entity.description: No consumption sensor is configured, so every plan assumes a flat household load of {fallback_w} W. Plans can be far off (too little energy saved for the evening, wrong hold/discharge decisions). Select your household consumption power or energy sensor under Configure → Consumption & grid (for Victron: the AC consumption sensor).

load_fallback_no_history.title: Energy Control found no consumption history
load_fallback_no_history.description: The recorder has no hourly statistics for {entity_id}, so every plan assumes a flat household load of {fallback_w} W. Make sure the sensor has a state class (measurement for power, total/total_increasing for energy) and is recorded; the forecast is rebuilt every few hours.

export_price_missing.title: Raw export price is missing
export_price_missing.description: Your contract uses spot compensation or switches to it within 60 days. The all-in source has no raw energy price. Supply a source with a spot component, explicitly configure a spot-only source, or choose the contracted fixed export price. Price-dependent battery export is blocked where the price is unknown; incomplete costs and savings are hidden.

pending_restores.title: Replaced actuators still need restoring
pending_restores.description: These original settings are persisted and retried every 30 seconds until readback confirms restoration. Check availability and units, or restore these exact values manually: {restores}

grid_constraints.title: Forecast grid limits cannot be satisfied
grid_constraints.description: Forecast demand exceeds the configured grid limit even with available battery assistance. Inspect grid_violation_kw and each slot reason. Check demand, battery capabilities and grid limits. The planner retains available assistance and explicitly reports unavoidable overload.

no_entry.message: No loaded Energy Control entry found.

override_needs_control.message: An override only works in a control mode (auto, self consumption, force charge/discharge, hold) with a grid setpoint configured; current mode: {mode}.

min_soc_above_max.message: Minimum SoC ({min_soc}%) cannot be above maximum SoC ({max_soc}%).

no_plan.message: There is no plan yet; wait for the first plan or check the price and SoC sensors.

no_window.message: No window of that length fits between the earliest start and the latest end within the known prices.
